newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia welcomes Yugoslav succession dialogue.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia welcomes Yugoslav succession dialogue.

text.p: Slovenia said on Wednesday it welcomed a newly established dialogue with rump Yugoslavia on the division of ex-Yugoslav assets although no agreement between the successor republics had been reached so far.

"The dialogue has started as this was our first meeting with Belgrade in the past years," Miran Mejak, chairman of the Slovenian Succession Commission, a governmental body dealing with succession issues, told Reuters.

The five successor states of the former Yugoslav federation met for the first time in Brussels this week under the guidance of Sir Arthur Watts, special negotiatior for succession issues at the office of international coordinator Carl Bildt.
"We reached no agreement but Yugoslavia at least started to consider several alternatives," Mejak said.
Until this week, rump Yugoslavia -- consisting of Serbia and Montenegro -- has refused to participate in the talks.
Yugoslavia's pre-1991 assets are estimated to total between $60 billion and $100 billion. The federation broke apart in a bloody conflict that started in 1991.

Representatives of the five states are scheduled to meet again in Brussels on November 11 and 12, but experts said Slovenia, Croatia, Bosnia and Macedonia were likely to hold a meeting prior to that in Zagreb to discuss a joint strategy.
Earlier this year rump Yugoslavia attempted to torpedo other successor republics' moves to settle their share of the former Yugoslavia's commercial debt, estimated at $4.3 billion.
Both Slovenia and Croatia have ignored legal challenges by Belgrade and completed separate rescheduling agreements with their London Club commercial creditors.
Resolving the debt problem is seen as a key condition for a successful conclusion of the succession talks.
